our_title: meshXD/torusXD loader accepts a dimension count below one, reading c[-1]
ran: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build/lib build/bin/gmap repro/COR-07/m4x4.grf repro/COR-07/meshx0.tgt /dev/null -> 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 ... #0 _SCOTCHarchMeshXDomNum arch_mesh.c:843 #1 _SCOTCHmapTerm mapping.c:495 #2 graphMapCompute2'. Same for 'meshXD -1' and 'torusXD 0'. Patched gmap: 'gmap: ERROR: archMeshXArchLoad: bad input (1)'.
severity_note: Heap OOB read reachable from any user .tgt file passed to gmap/atst; matches the review's medium. Only the meshXD half is this group's; the tleaf half is G02's.
evidence: archMeshXArchLoad only bounds dimnnbr above: 'if ((intLoad (stream, &archptr->dimnnbr) != 1) || (archptr->dimnnbr > ARCHMESHDIMNMAX))'. archMeshXDomNum starts 'domnnum = domnptr->c[archptr->dimnnbr - 1][0]' so dimnnbr==0 reads c[-1].
review_accuracy: accurate for the meshXD half (c[-1] read on 'meshXD 0'/'-1').
first_pass_critique: Correct status/evidence. Its option A bundled the tleaf fix (other group) and asked a Scotch-team question about levlnbr==0; for meshXD the lower bound is uncontroversial (a 0-dimension mesh is meaningless and already crashes). No separate critique.

fix_options.label: A. Reject dimnnbr < 1 at load time
fix_options.summary: Add '(archptr->dimnnbr < 1)' to the archMeshXArchLoad guard; fixes meshXD and torusXD (shared loader).
fix_options.tested: gmap on meshx0/meshxm1/torusx0 rejected with 'bad input (1)'; all valid m*/torus* targets still map; check_scotch_arch, check_prog_atst/amk/amk_grf/acpl/gmap pass 32/64-bit.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Behaviour change: 'meshXD 0' (previously a crash) now a clean load error.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches archMesh2ArchLoad/archMesh3ArchLoad which already reject c[i] < 1, and archHcubArchLoad which rejects dimnnbr < 1 (arch_hcub.c:105).

fix_options.label: B. Guard the consumers (DomNum/DomSize/...) for dimnnbr==0
fix_options.summary: Leave the loader permissive and special-case a 0-dimension architecture in every consumer.
fix_options.tested: untested: large audit surface (DomNum, DomSize, DomDist, Bipart, MatchInit, Save); negative counts and overflow would still need a load-time check, so B cannot replace A.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Much larger, error-prone; not what the tree does elsewhere.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He validates untrusted sizes at the loader, not in every consumer.

notes: One commit (0002) covers COR-07 and the mesh/torus/cmpltw half of COR-21; the deco part of COR-21 is in 0003.

our_title: meshXD distance folded like a torus (fixed upstream); torusX still folds by design
ran: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build/lib build/bin/atst on 'meshXD 2 8 8' -> 'A Distance ... max=14', identical to 'mesh2D 8 8'; 'meshXD 3 4 4 4' == 'mesh3D 4 4 4' (max=9); 'torusXD 2 8 8' still max=8 == 'torus2D 8 8' (correct for a torus).
severity_note: Was a silent wrong-objective bug; now fixed.
evidence: 7.0.17 archMeshXDomDist: 'disttmp = ((ABS (...) + 1) / 2); distval += disttmp;' with 'return (distval);' -- no wrap-around folding, consistent with archMesh2DomDist/archMesh3DomDist.
upstream_change: feecf0d 'Bugfix: make archMeshXDomDist() consistent with mesh distances [report R. Perry]' (and f545452 later switched abs() to ABS()).
first_pass_critique: First pass marked it 'fixed' correctly. It did not note that the twin archTorusXDomDist (arch_torus.c:169-176) KEEPS the folding on purpose (a torus has wrap-around links) -- verified: torusXD distances match torus2D/3D, so the twin is correct and must NOT be changed. The 7.0.17 rounding '(ABS(..)+1)/2' differs from the review's suggested 'distval += disttmp; >> 1' but gives the same tested results.
notes: No patch: completely fixed in 7.0.17, twin confirmed intentional.

our_title: Mesh/torus dimension products and cmpltw/deco weight sums overflow Anum from a .tgt file
ran: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build/lib build/bin/atst: 'mesh2D 65536 65536' -> 'arch_mesh.c:204:51: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 65536 * 65536'; 'mesh3D 2000 2000 2000' -> arch_mesh.c:480; 'meshXD 2 65536 65536' -> arch_mesh.c:891; torus twins identical; 'cmpltw 2 2000000000 2000000000' -> arch_cmpltw.c:259; 'deco 0 1 70000' -> arch_deco.c:261; 'deco 1 1 70000' -> arch_deco.c:304. Patched: all rejected with 'bad input'/'bad input (3)'/'bad input (2)'; 'cmplt 2147483647' still loads.
severity_note: UBSan signed overflow -> wrong terminal counts / bogus allocation sizes; low because such huge 32-bit architectures were never representable. Agrees with the review.
evidence: arch_mesh.c loaders checked only c[i] < 1, never the product; archMeshXArchLoad looped without a running product. arch_cmpltw.c archCmpltwArchLoad2: 'velosum += veloval' with no bound. arch_deco.c allocates '(((termdommax * (termdommax - 1)) / 2) + 1) * sizeof (Anum)' with termdommax unbounded.
review_accuracy: accurate; the review lists arch_mesh.c and arch_cmpltw.c. The same pattern also exists in arch_deco.c (termdommax products and the terminal-weight accumulation), which the review did not list.
first_pass_critique: First pass option A is essentially right and I adopted its idiom. Two issues: (1) it added the cmpltw overflow check ONLY in archCmpltwArchLoad2 and labelled both of its two hunks 'archCmpltwArchLoad2', but the twin accumulation in archCmpltwArchBuild2 (reached by SCOTCH_archCmpltw API) needs it too, with its own prefix -- I guard both; (2) it did not notice the arch_deco.c instances (termdommax product and terminal-weight sum).

fix_options.label: A. Validate at load time (reject)
fix_options.summary: Check each dimension product and weight sum against ANUMMAX with the 'a > ANUMMAX / b' idiom before computing it; bound termdommax so the deco distance matrix fits.
fix_options.tested: all listed inputs rejected before overflow, UBSan silent; valid targets and the compiled deco corpus unchanged; check_scotch_arch/_deco/_build and prog_atst/amk/amk_grf/acpl/gmap pass 32/64-bit.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Rejects .tgt files that used to load with wrapped (wrong) counts.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same 'bad input' chain he already uses in every ArchXxxLoad; the 'a > MAX / b' form matches the commGatherv overflow guard 73229e6.

fix_options.label: B. Widen the DomSize arithmetic and clamp
fix_options.summary: Compute products in int64_t and clamp to ANUMMAX in archMesh*DomSize, leaving the loaders permissive.
fix_options.tested: untested: clamping returns a silently wrong size and every consumer (mapping, coarsening) still sees an inconsistent architecture; does not address cmpltw/deco weight sums.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Hides the problem instead of rejecting; introduces int64_t into Anum paths.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He rejects bad input at the loader rather than silently clamping downstream.

notes: mesh/torus/cmpltw in 0002; the deco termdommax bound and terminal-weight overflow in 0003 (one commit owns arch_deco.c). Patch 0002's arch_cmpltw.c hunk is based on top of G25's patch 0001 (which fixes the memFree in archCmpltwArchBuild2); do not reorder before it.

our_title: Deco loader ignores build result and never validates compiled (type-1) data
ran: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build/lib build/bin/atst bad1.tgt (type-1, size 9 with no children) -> 'heap-buffer-overflow READ ... _SCOTCHarchDecoDomSize arch_deco.c:485'; gmap m4x4.grf bad1.tgt -> 'archDecoDomDist arch_deco.c:511'; a type-1 file with a negative distance -> 'stack-buffer-overflow ... graphMapView2 library_graph_map_view.c:473'; 'deco 0' duplicate-terminal file loads OK in release. Mutation fuzzer over amk_*/acpl corpus: 43 distinct sanitizer signatures pristine -> 0 memory-safety signatures patched. Patched: bad1 -> 'bad input (7)', dup0 -> 'bad terminal count', neg distance -> 'bad input (6)'.
severity_note: Raised from the review's medium: a user-supplied 'deco 1' .tgt file gives a heap AND a stack buffer overflow (not just OOB read), reachable through the public SCOTCH_archLoad and every tool; the type-0 result-drop additionally returns success on a freed architecture.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/arch_deco.c:297 (dropped return), 137-165,194-202 (Build2 checks under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1), 312-338 (type-1 loader, no validation)
evidence: 'archDecoArchBuild2 (archptr, termdomnbr, termdommax, termverttab, termdisttab);' at :297 ignores the result (and Build2 frees archptr on failure). Build2's 'bad maximum terminal' (:138), 'bad terminal count' (:161) and 'invalid null distance' (:196) are all inside '#ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1'. The type-1 branch reads domverttab/domdisttab with no size/tree/distance check.
review_accuracy: accurate; if anything understated -- the type-1 path also yields a stack-buffer-overflow in graphMapView2 via a negative distance (the histogram commdist[] clamps only the high side).
first_pass_critique: First pass option A is the right shape and I followed it, with corrections: (1) it used a magic 'termdommax <= 46340' literal; I use the overflow idiom '(termdommax - 1) > (ANUMMAX / termdommax)' which also scales to 64-bit; (2) it did not validate the type-1 DISTANCE array, missing the negative-distance stack-buffer-overflow in graphMapView2 -- I reject domdistval < 0; (3) it made the 'invalid null distance' check unconditional but left the terminal-weight accumulation unchecked (overflow). Its leaf check and type-1 tree check are correct and kept.

extra_instances.location: src/libscotch/arch_deco.c:337 type-1 distance read (negative distance -> graphMapView2 stack OOB)

fix_options.label: A. Propagate result, make Build2 checks unconditional, validate type-1 tree and distances
fix_options.summary: Check archDecoArchBuild2's return; make its num-range/terminal-count/null-distance checks unconditional (+free); reject a declared terminal that is not a leaf; bound termdommax; check the overall weight; validate type-1 size>=0, size>1 => sons in range summing, root==termdomnbr, distance>=0.
fix_options.tested: all malformed files rejected with clean errors; valid ok0/ok1 and the 7 compiled corpus/*_c1.tgt load identically to pristine; fuzzer 0 memory-safety hits; check_scotch_arch_deco and prog_amk/amk_grf/acpl/atst/gmap pass 32/64-bit; debug (-DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL) compiles.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Malformed deco files that used to load now fail. No valid file is rejected (0 distances for unused domains kept).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Loaders are where untrusted data enters; the unconditional 'bad input' rejection is exactly the discipline of d555f2c and the G01 arch-loader series.

fix_options.label: B. Minimal: only propagate the result (and type-1 tree)
fix_options.summary: Add just the return check in the loader; leave Build2's checks debug-only.
fix_options.tested: untested beyond compile: does not catch the type-0 duplicate/non-leaf inconsistencies in release (Build2 then fails only on OOM), so the PS-COR-1 OOB remains in release builds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Leaves the release-mode type-0 holes open.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would make the checks unconditional, as the data is user-controlled.

cleanup_done: none needed (the removed #ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1 blocks become unconditional; no symbol orphaned)
notes: Residual UBSan signed-overflows seen by the fuzzer after the fix are all downstream mapping-cost arithmetic (kgraph_map_rb.c:660, kgraph_map_rb_map.c:944, bgraph.c) from huge but self-consistent distances/weights -- shared by every architecture class, not a deco-loader defect; see extra.json PS2-G03-2 (info).

our_title: Type-0 deco terminal that is an ancestor of other terminals overflows the distance table
ran: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build/lib build/bin/atst repro/PS-COR-1/anc.tgt ('deco 0 4 4' with terminals numbered 1..4) -> 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ ... _SCOTCHarchDecoArchBuild2 arch_deco.c:193 #1 _SCOTCHarchDecoArchLoad arch_deco.c:297'. Patched: 'archDecoArchBuild2: terminal domain is not a leaf'.
severity_note: Heap OOB read from a user .tgt file; reachable on the release type-0 path (independent of debug flags).
evidence: When a declared terminal number is an interior node, after accumulation its size > 1, so the distance loop treats it as having subdomains and indexes archDecoArchDistE(archptr, 2*i, ...) with 2*i beyond termdommax.
review_accuracy: n/a (new defect found by the first pass, confirmed here).
first_pass_critique: First pass correctly found it and preferred the leaf check (option A). Its alternative 'bound the distance loop' hides the inconsistent tree rather than rejecting it; I agree with the leaf check and implement it.

fix_options.label: A. Leaf check after accumulation
fix_options.summary: After summing sizes to the root, require every declared terminal domain to have size 1; else error and free.
fix_options.tested: anc.tgt rejected; valid 'deco 0' files (ok0, amk corpus) unchanged; fuzzer clean.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: A leaf has size 1 by construction; checking it belongs with the other Build2 consistency checks the same commit makes unconditional.

fix_options.label: B. Bound the distance loop
fix_options.summary: Skip domains whose son index 2*j+1 exceeds termdommax in the distance loop.
fix_options.tested: untested: avoids the OOB but silently builds a distance matrix from an inconsistent tree, yielding wrong distances.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Masks the defect instead of rejecting the file.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He rejects inconsistent input rather than computing on it.

notes: Same commit as COR-16 (one deco-loader hardening commit).

our_title: fiboHeapDecreaseMacro body names the caller's variables, not its parameters
ran: Source-read plus build: fibo.h:153 '(treeptr->cmpfptr (nodeptr, pareptr) < 0)' and fibo.h:155/162 'fiboHeapMoveToRoot (treeptr, nodeptr, ...)' use treeptr/nodeptr. Single caller fibo.c:293 'fiboHeapDecreaseMacro (treeptr, nodeptr)'. After the (t)/(n) rename the full library builds with 0 warnings 32/64-bit and check_prog_amk/gmap (which exercise the Fibonacci heap via graph_diam.c) pass.
read_only: the latent misbehaviour (a caller using other variable names) cannot be exercised because the only caller uses matching names; verified by the rename compiling and behaving identically.
severity_note: Latent only; no runtime effect today (single caller uses the named variables). Agrees with the review.
evidence: Macro parameters are (t,n) but the body reads treeptr/nodeptr; it compiles only because fibo.c's fiboHeapDecrease uses those names.
first_pass_critique: First pass option A (pure rename) is right. Its sketch diff mangled the line-continuation backslash alignment; my commit keeps all backslashes aligned at their original column (90).

fix_options.label: A. Use the macro parameters
fix_options.summary: Replace treeptr->(t) and nodeptr->(n) in the body, including both fiboHeapMoveToRoot calls.
fix_options.tested: library builds 0 warnings 32/64-bit and under -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL; prog_amk/gmap pass; behaviour unchanged (single caller).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Zero behaviour change; removes a trap for future callers.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Consistent with the neighbouring macros (fiboHeapMoveToRoot, fiboHeapDelMacro) which all use their own parameters.

fix_options.label: B. Replace the macro with a static inline function
fix_options.summary: Turn fiboHeapDecrease into a static inline function to get parameter hygiene for free.
fix_options.tested: untested sketch (diff only switches the #define; a real change moves the body into a function).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Larger change; the maintainer deliberately keeps these hot-path operations as macros.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He keeps fibo operations as macros (fiboHeapUnlink/LinkAfter/Del); a one-token rename is closer to his habit.

notes: Every fiboHeapDecrease user checked: fibo.c:293, graph_diam.c:180, check/test_fibo.c:232 -- all go through the macro with matching names, so the rename is safe.

our_title: dummysizes dereferences unset file names; broken debug block and line-length test
ran: build/src/libscotch/dummysizes (ASan+UBSan): './dummysizes < /dev/null' -> 'dummysizes.c:229:30: runtime error: load of null pointer of type char' then SEGV; one-arg form same; a 2046-char line wrongly reported 'line too long'; '-DSCOTCH_DEBUG_MAIN1' did not compile (C_fileTab[i].name/.pntr absent). Patched: both no-arg/one-arg forms exit 0, the 2046-char line accepted, and it compiles with -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_MAIN1; the full library still builds (scotch.h/ptscotch.h regenerated at build time).
severity_note: Build-time helper only, not shipped in the installed library; the Makefile/CMake always pass two names so the build never hits the crash. Agrees with the review.
evidence: 'static File C_fileTab[C_FILENBR] = {{FILEMODER},{FILEMODEW}}' leaves nameptr NULL; the default loop set only fileptr; then 'C_fileTab[i].nameptr[0]' is read for every i. The length test reads chartab[CHARMAX-1] (a slot fgets never fills). The debug block uses C_fileTab[i].name/.pntr, which do not exist in File (nameptr/fileptr).
first_pass_critique: First pass option A (default names to '-') is right and tested; it did NOT actually apply the other two fixes the review calls for (the CHARMAX-2 line test and the debug-block field names). I include all three in one commit, as the review recommends.

fix_options.label: A. Default names to '-', fix the line test and the debug block
fix_options.summary: Set nameptr='-' in the default loop; test chartab[CHARMAX-2]; refer to nameptr/fileptr in the SCOTCH_DEBUG_MAIN1 block.
fix_options.tested: no-arg/one-arg exit 0; 2046-char line accepted, over-long line still rejected; builds with and without -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_MAIN1; full scotch+ptscotch build regenerates the headers with 0 warnings.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Every other tool defaults names to '-' via fileBlockInit (common_file.c:177); dummysizes predates that helper and simply forgot.

fix_options.label: B. Require both file names
fix_options.summary: Exit with usage if fewer than two names are given.
fix_options.tested: untested: contradicts the documented '[in [out]]' optional-argument usage; does not fix the debug block or line test.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: The documented usage marks both names optional, so defaulting them is the in-style fix.

notes: dummysizes is the build-time header generator invoked by both the Makefile and CMake with two names; verified the fix keeps both build paths working by building the library.
